what: Giri Gosains, wealthy celibate 'semi-hermit' Brahman zamindars of Sherpur; line kept by adoption (religious adoption of disciples), matted hair, cast away sacred thread on joining; considerable landed property.
quote: Two peculiar classes of semi-hermit celibate Brahmans are found in this district, known as Giri Gosains and Kanphatha Jogis.

what: Giri Gosains: said originally Dravidian Brahmans, now recruit by adoption from Bengali Brahman septs; present two representatives Gaur Brahmans, predecessor a Rarhi.
quote: They are said to have belonged originally to the Dravidian division of Brabmaus, but now keep up their line by adoption from any of the septs of Bengali Brahmans.

what: Giri Gosains' ascetic marks: minimal clothing, artificially matted hair, discard of the paita (sacred thread) on entering the life.
quote: They used to wear as little clothing as sufficed to cover their nakedness, artificially matted their hair, and even now cast away the paitd or sacred Brahmanical thread on joining their new life.

what: Sherpur's principal landholders include the Giri Gosains (with Sanyals, Munshis). First Giri Gosain at Sherpur was Dan; second by religious adoption Raghunath Giri Gosain managed Raja Prannath Rai of Dighapatia's property, leased estate Naokhila in east Bogra, amassed a fortune; two disciple-heirs spent Rs 15,000 each on his sraddha (c. 1800). Family still holds considerable landed property.
quote: The first Giri Gosain who settled in Sherpur was named Dan.

what: Kanphatha Jogis: priests of the ancient shrine of Jogir Bhuban, followers of Gorakhnath; ear-slitting at initiation; buried in own houses.
quote: The Kanphathas profess to be followers of Gorakhnath.

what: 1777: 200 Nagas, 'up-country religious fanatics', came from the north-west, met Majnu Fakir's dacoits and destroyed them in battle (Fakirkata khal near Champapur); then went to Mymensingh and Goalpara.
quote: In 1777, a body of Nagas, a caste of up-country religious fanatics, to the number of two hundred, came to this district, from the north-west

what: Majnu Fakir and gang terrorised Bogra in the last quarter of the 18th century; son Cherag Ali Fakir continued. Dacoit fakirs (Muslim).
quote: The most notorious ddkdit of these parts was one Majnu Fakir, who with his gang spread havoc and ruin in this part of the province

what: Rent-free tenures: Vaishnabottar (6 tenures in 1901) for Vishnu devotees; Sannyasottar granted for support of sannyasis or religious ascetics (number not given); also fakiran, piran, debottar.
quote: Sannydsotture were granted for the support of Sannydaia or religious ascetics.

what: Gossainbari (market, Dhunot thana): place-name; no ascetic order stated.
quote: flows past the flourishing and important marts of Gossainbari and Barabila

what: A Vaisnab mendicant has established himself on a stupa at the old fort (place not named in the passage).
quote: on the top of which a Vaisnab mendicant has established himself.

what: Jugis: low-caste weavers (3,318), bury their dead; most abandoned weaving for agriculture. Weaver caste, not ascetic.
quote: Amongst these are the Jugis, or weavers, remarkable amongst Hindus for burying their dead ;
